Samir: Quick heads-up — profiler on canary shows ~3x tail when kernel fallback coincides with KV miss. Need a per-request link from the token-latency panel to the trace viewer so we can correlate. Anyone else seeing this pattern?

Priya: I saw the same cluster last night around 03:12Z. I grabbed a trace: trace_id=abcd1234. Looks like multiple small batches hit the fallback kernel and we get an extra ~8ms per-token on the tail.

Diego: Pulled the profiler and a flame sample. Fallback path does an extra kernel init + memcpy. snippet from the log:
```
[runtime] kernel_select: chosen=fast_fp16 fallback=slow_int8
[runtime] kv_cache: miss for prefix_key=0x7f8a...
[perf] memcpy 0.122ms, kernel_init 6.8ms
```

Priya: Also noticed KV misses spike when batch_size > 8 for route /chat/completions. Our batching heuristic probably groups heterogeneous seq-lens and pushes some requests into the fallback path.

Claire: Proposal: propagate request_id as a top-level trace/span id and emit token-level spans (cache.lookup, kernel.exec, token.encode). Then add a small "Open trace" action on the token-latency panel that navigates to /traces/{request_id}. That should make root-cause fast.

Samir: Agreed. We should also add per-route KPIs: p50/p95/p99 tokens/ms, kv-hit-rate, and fallback-count. Current dashboards only show aggregated host-level metrics which hide these cases. :eyes:  

InfraBot: deploy:perf-instrumentation v2 deployed to canary at 1979997778 :rocket:

Diego: I pushed a runtime change to attach X-Req-ID and emit lightweight token spans to the telemetry pipeline. Code snippet: 
```python
# runtime handler
req_id = headers.get('X-Req-ID') or generate_req_id()
tracer.set_tag('request.id', req_id)
emit_span('token.cache_lookup', {'req': req_id})
```

Priya: Running the perf harness now against the canary. Initial 1h sample looks promising: kv-hit-rate went from 68% -> 79% for /chat when batching tuned to prefer same-seqlen grouping. Will dump numbers in the perf dashboard tomorrow morning.

Claire: FYI I found a subtle regression path: kernel selector prefers the "lowest avg latency" kernel but that policy doesn't account for long sequence tails, so for sequences > 1024 tokens it sometimes picks a kernel with worse tail behavior. Opening an RFC to add sequence-length-aware scores.

Samir: Action items: (1) Add trace-link button to token-latency panel (2) Surface kv-hit-rate & fallback-count per route (3) Roll the X-Req-ID/token-spans change to prod if canary stability holds. @Diego can you post the PR link?

Diego: PR here: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/462 — adds X-Req-ID propagation and token-level spans. Requesting reviews from @Priya and @Claire.

Priya: :thumbsup: I'll review today and run the extended harness overnight. If p99 improves or stays flat, we can greenlight.

Claire: Also recommend an alert rule: fire when kv-hit-rate < 75% AND p99 tokens/ms increases > 20% for 5m. Will draft in dash infra.

Samir: Thanks team — I'll update the dashboard ticket with the trace link mock and the per-route KPI list, and follow up with the canary report in the morning.
